questions.passage: Why do rusty-spotted cats purr but lions roar? Researchers hypothesize that this difference between the two feline species may be partly due to a U-shaped bone in their throats called the hyoid. Rusty- spotted cats, which are much smaller than lions, have a rigid hyoid that rumbles when the cat's larynx vibrates, resulting in a purr. By contrast, lions have a somewhat flexible hyoid, and the bone is attached to the skull with a stretchy ligament that rusty-spotted cats lack. These traits allow lions and most other species of big cats to produce powerful roars. The same traits may also prevent most big cats from purring.
questions.prompt: According to the text, which trait do researchers think may contribute to a rusty-spotted cat's ability to purr?

choices.A: The ligament attaching the hyoid bone to the rusty-spotted cat's skull.
choices.B: The relative size of the rusty-spotted cat's body and throat.
choices.C: The rusty-spotted cat's rigid hyoid bone.
choices.D: The shape of the rusty-spotted cat's larynx.
